faq.a: A Systematic Investment Plan (SIP) is a method of investing a fixed amount of money regularly into a mutual fund scheme, typically monthly. It helps in disciplined investing and benefits from rupee cost averaging.

faq.q: How does compounding help in wealth creation?
faq.a: Compounding allows your investment returns to generate further returns, creating a snowball effect. The longer your investment horizon, the more significant the impact of compounding on your wealth accumulation.

faq.q: Which mutual fund type is best for building a ₹1 crore corpus?
faq.a: For long-term goals like a ₹1 crore corpus, equity-oriented funds (like large-cap, multi-cap, or aggressive hybrid funds) are often recommended due to their potential for higher returns over extended periods, though they come with higher risk.

faq.q: Can I increase my SIP amount over time?
faq.a: Yes, you can opt for a "Step-up SIP" or simply increase your monthly contribution as your income grows. Increasing your SIP regularly can significantly accelerate your journey towards your ₹1 crore goal.

Rupee cost averaging is a strategy where you invest a fixed amount regularly, buying more units when prices are low and fewer when prices are high. This averages out your purchase cost over time and mitigates market timing risk.

The adequacy of ₹1 crore for retirement depends entirely on your lifestyle, expenses, and inflation over time. It's crucial to consider inflation-adjusted expenses and consult a financial planner to determine a truly sufficient retirement corpus.

faq.q: Are there tax implications on mutual fund returns?
faq.a: Yes, returns from mutual funds are subject to taxation. Equity-oriented funds have Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) tax at 10% on gains above ₹1 lakh in a financial year (after 1 year holding) and Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) tax at 15% (if held for less than 1 year). Debt funds are taxed as per your income tax slab for short-term gains and at 20% with indexation benefit for long-term gains. You can find more details on the Income Tax India website.
